- If sentiment shows strong positive bias (e.g., >0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shows strong negative bias (e.g., <0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 2–3 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 75% of recent high), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently > true outcome by >3% over 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction (e.g., subtract 0.5–1.5% per day).  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., 1.00, -0.33, 0.33), model may be overfitting; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.  
- For horizon > 14 days, model tends to overestimate; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for long-term forecasts.  
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after model spike, model may be ignoring sentiment; adjust forecast to align with sentiment trend, not just price history.
